First, for context: the first TES game I played was Daggerfall, when it was current.

Oblivion is my favorite, but I think that Morrowind is the best.

TES games have followed a pattern through pretty much their entire history. Each new game has been prettier and shinier than the previous games, and each new game (with the arguable exception of Daggerfall) has had less content, fewer alternatives and fewer roleplaying elements than the previous game(s). They've been constantly visually upgraded and constantly streamlined.

Daggerfall is actually the most satisfying one to play, from a roleplaying perspective, just because that game is so rich and the character building alternatives are so complex. It's really a bit much in my opinion though. It's comparatively difficult to play (and not helped by the fact that it's buggy). I think, and thought at the time, that the Daggerfall to Morrowind transition was the one time that the combination of improving visuals and mechanics and sacrificing gameplay complexity was worthwhile.

Morrowind, IMO, strikes the most impressive balance between the two. It still retains enough complexity to be very rewarding and to make for a lot of variety, but in a more stable and more accessible package. And the world-building of Morrowind is tremendous - Morrowind is a wholly alien environment that's so well presented (even with the fairly primitive graphics) that it feels as if I've actually been there, walking around and soaking it all in.

But, sort of oddly, my favorite is Oblivion. I was actually disappointed with Oblivion on release, because I felt (and in fact still feel) that Beth took the streamlining too far. I detest the quest arrows and the in-game walkthrough posing as a journal, and I loathe the fact that this enormous game has only four main factions with (by previous standards) relatively uninspiring quest lines. There are too few skills with too little impact on the game (and zero impact on the factions) and leveling is too quick and too easy.

But the thing with Oblivion... in the background of that relative lack of content and overabundant handholding is a fairly complex and more notably VERY open world. A lot of that is the much (and inaccurately) maligned level scaling. When I play Oblivion, I can create just about any character I could possibly imagine and take him/her out into the world and watch as s/he lives some sort of life in Cyrodiil. Particularly as I've come to value roleplaying ever more, I find it to be the most rewarding one to play. Yes - it would be much better if it had the depth and complexity of the factions and character development options of Morrowind, much less Daggerfall, but it has enough that I can at least get something out of it, and most to the point, it has a world that is inviting to the odd and quirky characters I've come to prefer playing. That's a problem with Morrowind (and even more so with Daggerfall) - there's more opportunity to create more complex characters, but it's more of a struggle to keep the really quirky ones alive in those relatively dangerous worlds. It's more satisfying in a way when I succeed, but it takes more effort, so I'm less likely to even try. When I want to create a really interesting character and follow along with an interesting life, Oblivion is easily the best of the lot to do it in.
